title: Pure-section formulas for native complex tensor constraints
statement: Let C be a category with object universe c and morphism universe v, J a Grothendieck topology on C, and R a commutative-ring sheaf in max(c,v,u). Assume additive sheafification and the locally bijective characterization of its local equivalences at that universe. Give R-module sheaves with sections in max(c,v,u) their canonical sheafification tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and give their unbounded cochain complexes the signed direct-sum total tensor. Let P,Q,N be arbitrary such complexes. On coefficientTensorGenerator(x,y) [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model] in total degree p+q, the native complex braiding is (-1)^(pq) times coefficientTensorGenerator(y,x). The native associator sends the nested pure generator (x tensor y) tensor z to x tensor (y tensor z) in every compatible triple degree. The native left and right unitors send the degree-zero ring section a tensored with a section x, in either order, to a*x. These four formulas use the actual tensor-sheafification comparison and single-complex degree-zero comparison; no K-flatness is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0FPQ, including its unit and coherence hints; More on Algebra, sign rules.

proof.text: The presheaf-to-sheaf functor is braided strong monoidal. Its right-adjoint forgetful functor has lax tensorator equal to the sheafification unit followed by the inverse tensor-sheafification comparison; this is the pairing in coefficientTensorGenerator. The triangle identity makes its unit map the identity on the ring presheaf.
Apply the lax braidedness equation to the presheaf pure tensor x tensor y, then the formula for complex braiding on a (p,q) summand. The result is (-1)^(pq) times the generator with factors reversed.

Apply lax associativity to (x tensor y) tensor z and the total associator formula on a (p,q,r) summand. Naturality moves the inner summand inclusions through the pairing. The result is the nested generator x tensor (y tensor z), without any interchange or sign.

Use the complex unitor inverse formula on its sole degree-zero unit summand. The single-complex comparison carries a to the indicated degree-zero section. Lax unitality of the forgetful functor reduces both unitors to the ordinary module unitors, which send a tensor x and x tensor a to a*x. Apply the inverse identities to obtain the formulas for their forward maps. No elementwise generation claim for global sections after sheafification is required; these are identities on the specified pure sections only.
